recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if a new work-group issue asks to introduce distinct expired or incomplete statuses; FHIR-20767 itself is already correctly reflected.
issue_request: FHIR-20767 asked to add terminal QuestionnaireResponseStatus codes for "incomplete" and "expired". The final Published/Not Persuasive with Modification resolution instead required changing the existing "stopped" definition to say no subsequent changes can be made, treating that as the terminal incomplete-with-answers case and rejecting a no-answer expired QuestionnaireResponse use case.
initial_application: Git commit 62958938b9c71812294149adf3dbb678e8ac2b00, also recorded in a Jira comment, changed source/questionnaireresponse/codesystem-questionnaire-answers-status.xml so the stopped code definition ends with "No subsequent changes can be made."
additional_context: QuestionnaireResponse is active in source/fhir.ini, QuestionnaireResponse.status is required-bound to ValueSet/questionnaire-answers-status, and that ValueSet includes the complete questionnaire-answers-status CodeSystem. The current CodeSystem has the terminal stopped wording and no separate incomplete or expired codes, which is consistent with the final resolution. FHIR-12315 is the older background issue that introduced stopped; it was not separately decided because the seed only required auditing the later clarification.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative current source already carries the required stopped definition, and related Jira/Zulip/Confluence searches found no later or conflicting decision requiring separate incomplete or expired codes.
